title: Opportunities and challenges of generative AI in the research lifecycle
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored and adopted across the research lifecycle, from idea generation and literature discovery to data analysis, manuscript preparation, and editorial and peer-review processes. This perspective provides an overview of AI’s role across the stages of scientific research. We describe emerging tools and workflows, illustrating how AI can assist researchers by aggregating and synthesizing a large body of work across various domains, supporting methodological implementation, and facilitating communication and publication. We also discuss their shortcomings, including surface-level reasoning, the fabrication of plausible but incorrect outputs, and the challenges posed by the fact that researchers new to a field may not know which questions to ask or which nuances to interrogate. In addition, we discuss recent advances toward more agentic and end-to-end AI systems, highlighting both their technical feasibility and the challenges they pose for validation, oversight, and responsible use. For each stage of the research lifecycle, we outline key limitations of current AI systems and propose practical considerations, what researchers should and should not do to support rigorous and ethical integration of AI into scientific workflows. This integration requires coordinated frameworks across the ecosystem. Journals, funding agencies, universities, and policymakers play essential roles in defining standards for transparency and accountability, while individual researchers remain responsible for methodological rigor and validity of reported results.

title: Stop the spark detecting violence instigating Bangla text using ViolenceBanglaBERT
abstract: Abstract Due to the low cost and widespread availability of the internet and digital devices, the utilization of social networks is rapidly increasing. Therefore, in recent years, a group of individuals from different religions and cultural backgrounds has used social network platforms to promote misinformation and hatred, which has instigated communal violence and devastating consequences. Regarding this concerning rise of communal violence instigated through social media texts, this study presents a comprehensive benchmarking and optimization framework of multiple deep learning and transformer-based models for violence-instigating Bangla text classification. A wide range of embedding methods, deep learning architectures, transformer-based models, and existing approaches are systematically evaluated under a unified experimental framework. To address class imbalance, data augmentation via back-translation is applied to improve generalization. The experimental results illustrate that the proposed ViolenceBanglaBERT model, a fine-tuned version of a transformer-based classifier, achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.75 on the test set, outperforming other classifiers and existing approaches. The source code used in this study can be accessed at https://github.com/prosenjit-ch/SS-VIBTI .

title: From Monolithic Blending to Agentic Orchestration: Dynamic Response for Conversational Assistants at Scale
abstract: Conversational assistants can blend retrieval, action selection, escalation, and wording in a single model path, or separate those roles. We report a production migration of a customer-support assistant at a large accommodation marketplace (millions of conversations per month, 11 languages, 10-second P90). Dynamic Response (DR) replaces a single Qwen3-235B-A22B blended responder with a bounded ReAct orchestrator over typed tools plus a smaller generator that writes from a backend-validated context contract. Because the migration also changed prompts, alignment, and serving, we attribute each effect to its cause and claim as architecture effects only those measured on identical replayed turns: typed entity selection moves the reservation selector to a precision-first operating point (precision 8.3% to 89.1%, recall 75.2% to 67.3%), and typed action IDs with a membership check remove observed structured-action hallucination (2.14% to 0.0%). A low-ramp A/B test reproduces the replay escalation reductions: hard-escalation responses fall from 5.60% to 3.08% and soft-escalation responses from 9.56% to 2.49%, while production handoff volume holds roughly steady; self-solve is directional (+5.1 points, 95% CI [-2, +12]). Serving optimizations cut orchestrator P90 latency from 3.87s to 2.24s on a GPU footprint reduced by roughly one-third, and self-hosting reduces estimated annual model-serving cost by more than an order of magnitude.

title: From Matrices to Morphisms II: Examples of Computational Categories in MATLAB and Octave
abstract: This article develops the notion of a computational category, motivated by the observation that many mathematical structures occurring in scientific computing already admit concrete algorithmic representations. Finite sets, finite-dimensional vector spaces, relations, and graphs may all be represented through elementary MATLAB and Octave data structures such as indexing vectors, matrices, logical arrays, and sparse matrices. The central idea is that a category may often be described through a category of canonical representatives indexed by the natural numbers. This viewpoint leads naturally to representative categories whose objects are dimensions and whose morphisms are finite computational data structures. The resulting framework unifies several examples, including matrix categories, index categories, categories of column spaces, row-based models of finite sets, and categories combining finite subsets with finite-dimensional vector spaces through mixed morphisms. The paper also introduces computational categories with distinguished non-finite representatives, extending the finite setting while retaining concrete coordinate descriptions. Throughout, categorical constructions are interpreted algorithmically and implemented using standard MATLAB and Octave operations. The work contributes to a computational perspective on category theory and, conversely, to a categorical understanding of matrix-oriented scientific computing.

title: A Cost-Aware Agentic Architecture for NL-to-SQL over Nested Enterprise Schemas, with a New Benchmark
abstract: Natural-language-to-SQL systems have ad- vanced rapidly on academic benchmarks, yet production enterprise schemas exhibit graph- like, semi-structured, deeply nested structure that current benchmarks do not measure. We make two complementary contributions. First, we introduce the DevRev NL2SQL bench- mark: 900 execution-verified queries with nested-type and link-graph structure, accom- panied by the Semantic Depth Score (SDS), a schema-agnostic rubric for analytical reasoning depth. Second, we present a cost-aware single- generation agentic architecture whose schema- selection, metadata-retrieval, and error-repair components are designed for the requirements this regime imposes. On the DevRev NL2SQL benchmark the system attains 91.7% answer correctness, a margin of 54.6 percentage points over the next-best baseline; on the Spider 2.0 Snowflake public dataset, it is competitive with leading systems at a single-generation operating point.

title: Quantum Information Topological Field Theory
abstract: Quantum information theory has long been considered a promising avenue for advancing computational capabilities, particularly in the realm of quantum computing. However, existing quantum computing paradigms often rely on the manipulation of discrete quantum states and the execution of specific quantum gates. This research proposes a novel theoretical framework, the Quantum Information Topological Field Theory (QITFT), which explicitly integrates quantum entanglement with topological fields, offering a fundamentally new approach to computation. We aim to explore how the interplay between these two phenomena can lead to enhanced computational properties and a potential expansion of the quantum computing landscape. This work focuses on the core mechanisms of constructing a quantum computation process centered around the exploitation of quantum entanglement and topological field alignment. The current design incorporates a quantum entanglement-induced topological field formation, which is hypothesized to yield enhanced computational capabilities. This theory represents a departure from traditional quantum computing approaches, potentially addressing long-standing challenges and opening new avenues for algorithmic design.

title: Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Adjustment Strategy Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum machine learning (QML) to parameter adjustment within the training process of classical machine learning models. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on fixed adjustments, failing to effectively leverage complex, dynamic information derived from model training. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum algorithms to dynamically adjust model parameters based on both model training error and gradient information, promoting more robust and accurate model performance. This method integrates quantum error analysis into the parameter adjustment process, offering a fundamentally new approach to optimization. The research explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency and adaptability of parameter optimization, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical methods. This work focuses on the design and implementation of a QML-based parameter adjustment strategy, incorporating quantum algorithms for error assessment and dynamic parameter refinement. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to improve model generalization and robustness.

title: Ledger Vouching: Grounding Someone Else's Agent over the Wire
abstract: Tool-using LLM agents ship reports whose load-bearing values — numbers, identifiers, quantities — are frequently fabricated in-head: across two model generations, each measured under its own value-dense reporting demand, the per-token fabrication rate collapsed while the rate of episodes shipping at least one unverified value stayed at 75–81%. We present ledger vouching: an OpenAI-protocol proxy (the ledger voucher), adopted by changing one base_url line, compiles everything it observes on the wire into an observation ledger and deterministically vouches every load-bearing value in its extracted class (digit-bearing tokens: numbers, dates, prices, quantities, alphanumeric identifiers) in an agent's terminal answer to that ledger — no harness cooperation, and no verdict authority for any model: the ledger voucher itself enumerates verified candidate origins by reverse lookup against the ledger, and the model only selects among them for the audit trail. Enforcement is a three-mode ladder — flag, block (honest refusal), and retry (a close-gate keep-alive that pushes the agent to ground its own answer inside the protocol) — with a mandatory explicit fail posture; the guarantee is existence-semantics provenance, never correctness, with its residual refusal families stated and measured. Across two environments and two model generations we measure: transparency from byte level to operational (Δ = 0.000); zero unverified-value shipping in block mode (0/16 and 0/16 in live runs across generations under the enforced predicate, with the refusal cost quantified alongside; 814/814 fabricated-token recall against a privileged oracle in replay); honest, graceful degradation of retry on weak models alongside one-round convergence on a capable one; deterministic cost amplification (1.0×/2.0×/3.0×); and 13% directional agreement with an LLM judge that prefers fabricated answers in 10% of pairs. A companion paper reports that preference training on the same deterministic verifier's labels failed to reduce fabrication while a zero-training environment contract succeeded; the prescription our combined evidence supports is contract plus deterministic enforcement at the boundary.

title: Title: Quantum Decoherence Shielding (QDS)
abstract: Quantum Decoherence is a significant and persistent challenge in the field of quantum computing, hindering the development of practical quantum systems. This research investigates a novel shielding technique, Quantum Field Resonance Shielding (QDS), to actively mitigate this issue. We propose a method to generate a localized region of reduced decoherence through the precise manipulation of quantum fields, offering a proactive solution to the fundamental obstacle to quantum information processing. This work details the theoretical framework, implementation steps, and experimental validation of the QDS protocol, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance the stability and performance of quantum systems. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the underlying principles and potential applications of QDS.

title: Dynamic Quantum Computing Resource Allocation and Scheduling Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic quantum computing resource allocation and scheduling, addressing the limitations of static resource management in the field. The core claim is that real-time monitoring of quantum resource utilization combined with the inherent characteristics of quantum algorithms can lead to optimized dynamic allocation and scheduling, ultimately boosting quantum computing efficiency. The proposed mechanism leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to learn an optimal resource allocation policy. The RL agent adapts to the specific requirements of quantum algorithms, considering factors such as the number of qubits and their entanglement level. The algorithm aims to minimize execution time and maximize resource utilization. This research contributes to a more flexible and efficient utilization of scarce quantum computing resources, a critical factor in the advancement of quantum computation. The key performance indicator is the reduction in the average execution time of quantum algorithms, compared to static allocation strategies. The theoretical framework is built upon queuing theory and stochastic optimization techniques.

title: Algorithmic Bias Detection and Mitigation in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data, preserving data privacy. However, this approach is increasingly recognized to be vulnerable to algorithmic bias. The inherent diversity and potential imbalances within the data contributed by numerous clients can significantly impact the fairness and equity of the resulting global model. This paper investigates the propagation and amplification of biases in federated learning systems. We propose a framework for detecting and mitigating these biases by integrating differential privacy and fairness constraints into the training process. The core claim is that FL systems are inherently susceptible to bias propagation. The proposed mechanism involves monitoring model performance across client subgroups, quantifying bias metrics, and adjusting the training process to enforce fairness. This work contributes to the development of more robust and trustworthy FL systems, paving the way for responsible and equitable AI applications.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Models (DPF) – Extended
abstract: Dynamic Probability Field Models (DPF) represent a powerful framework for probabilistic modeling, enabling prediction by dynamically adjusting probability distributions based on environmental changes. This paper explores an extended DPF concept that introduces a "variable parameter" mechanism, enhancing its adaptability and precision in complex environments. We outline the core principles, theoretical foundation, and potential applications of this enhanced DPF, emphasizing the novelty of the variable parameter approach and its implications for improved predictive accuracy.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子几何验证
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology in quantum geometry to validate quantum systems, offering a novel approach to quantum computation verification. We propose a framework leveraging quantum computation's inherent properties to explore the complex topology that might emerge in quantum systems, ultimately providing a more robust and efficient quantum verification tool. The core claim is that establishing a self-adaptive topology in quantum geometry will yield a more accurate and reliable assessment of quantum system behavior, thereby enhancing the quality of quantum computations. This research focuses on utilizing quantum algorithms to identify and quantify topological features, offering a shift towards a more systematic and predictive verification process. This work introduces a new methodology for quantum geometry validation, incorporating adaptive techniques to improve the robustness and accuracy of verification procedures.

title: Algorithmic Co-evolution in Evolutionary Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, Algorithmic Co-evolution, designed to enhance the performance of evolutionary algorithms by incorporating a feedback loop between the algorithm's parameters and the outcomes of previous iterations. Traditional evolutionary approaches often rely on a single, fixed evolutionary process, limiting their capacity to explore complex solution spaces and achieve optimal performance. We propose a system where the algorithm iteratively refines its parameters based on the results of previous steps, fostering a self-improvement mechanism. This approach, termed Co-evolution, creates a continuous feedback loop that surpasses the inherent limitations of traditional methods, leading to improved solutions for complex optimization problems. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the problem's constraints and objective function based on the algorithm's output, driving a self-evolving solution space. This paper presents a detailed exploration of the Co-evolution algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary results on a challenging problem involving multi-objective optimization.

title: Title: Bayesian Network for Dynamical Systems in High-Dimensional Space
abstract: This research investigates the application of Bayesian Networks (BNs) to model and predict the evolution of complex, multi-variable dynamical systems within high-dimensional spaces. Traditional probabilistic models often fall short in effectively capturing the intricate dependencies and inherent uncertainty present in such systems. We propose a novel Bayesian Network architecture that explicitly models uncertainty as a latent variable, leveraging variational inference for efficient exploration of the network's state space. This approach offers a more robust and principled framework for handling high dimensionality, leading to improved prediction accuracy and a deeper understanding of the underlying dynamics. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically updated latent variable that influences the probabilities of different future states, ensuring a continuous representation of uncertainty. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to accurately predict system behavior in challenging high-dimensional scenarios.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Calculation Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential to revolutionize computation. This paper explores the design of a novel calculation model predicated on entanglement, aiming to accelerate complex calculations through the exploitation of this quantum property. We introduce the concept of 'entangled states' as a core mechanism, utilizing their unique characteristics to facilitate parallel processing and enhanced computational efficiency. The model's core claim centers around the ability to leverage entanglement to significantly reduce computational complexity compared to traditional methods. This research will detail the proposed model's architecture, the mathematical framework underpinning its operation, and preliminary results demonstrating its potential for advanced calculations. We will also address challenges and future directions for this burgeoning field.

title: 基于动态图的逻辑推演算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to logical reasoning, utilizing a dynamic graph representation to enhance efficiency in handling large-scale inference problems. Traditional logical reasoning algorithms often struggle with the complexity of large instances. Our algorithm leverages a dynamic graph to simulate the reasoning process, employing self-adaptive mechanisms to optimize performance. This work introduces a method to dynamically adjust the graph structure and reasoning steps, significantly improving the scalability and efficiency of logical inference. The core mechanism focuses on the iterative refinement of the graph based on the current state of the inference, resulting in a more robust and adaptable system. The proposed algorithm offers a promising avenue for addressing challenges in complex logical tasks.

title: 基于深度学习的非线性信号处理的动态泛化模型
abstract: This paper explores the application of deep learning to dynamic signal processing, focusing on the development of a novel model designed to effectively mitigate generalization errors across diverse datasets. Traditional signal processing methods often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability to complex, non-linear data distributions. We propose a dynamic, adaptive deep learning framework that learns robust representations and dynamically adjusts its parameters to better suit the specific characteristics of each input. The core of this approach lies in leveraging deep neural networks to automatically extract and refine key features, thereby enabling more robust and accurate signal processing. This research addresses a critical challenge in signal analysis – the need for models capable of handling complex, non-linear data – and presents a promising pathway toward improved performance in a variety of real-world applications.

title: A Multi-Strategy Enhanced Crested Porcupine Optimizer with Targeted Defense Mechanism Improvement for Global Optimization
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are widely used to solve complex optimization problems, but the trade-off between exploration and exploitation often limits their performance. The Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) employs four bio-inspired defense mechanisms and achieves competitive performance, but it still tends to converge prematurely, initialize populations poorly, and rely on static parameters that cannot adapt to different phases. This paper proposes a Multi-Strategy Enhanced Crested Porcupine Optimizer (MSCPO) with four phase-targeted enhancement strategies: (1) Kent Chaos Opposition-Based Learning Initialization (KCOL) improves the initial population distribution through chaotic-weighted reflection; (2) Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO)-Inspired Dual-Modal Evasion (APO-DME) reduces dependence on the global best solution and increases population diversity through dual-mode differential perturbation; (3) Adaptive Dual-Differential Perturbation (ADDP) refines the search by combining population diversity and elite guidance information; (4) Periodic Dynamic Adaptive Perturbation (PDAP) enhances exploitation through periodic trigonometric perturbation and a fitness-conditioned update rule. These strategies interact across the optimization process to strengthen each defense mechanism at the appropriate phase. On the CEC 2017 and CEC 2022 benchmark suites, MSCPO achieves the best overall mean rank among all compared algorithms, with an overall rank of 2.638 on CEC 2017 and 2.375 on CEC 2022. A full-factorial ablation over all 16 strategy combinations confirms that each strategy contributes positively: removing any single strategy degrades the overall mean rank, and the complete MSCPO achieves the best mean rank (3.34), significantly outperforming all single-strategy variants (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To verify the practical applicability of MSCPO, the algorithm is further applied to three engineering design problems: step-cone pulley design, hydrostatic thrust bearing design, and robotic gripper design. MSCPO ranks first on the hydrostatic thrust bearing problem, second on the step-cone pulley problem, and third on the robotic gripper problem. Future work will explore adaptive population sizing to further improve the scalability of MSCPO on very high-dimensional problems.

title: Tight Lower Bounds for State Tomography with Limited Entanglement
abstract: We study state tomography when each measurement acts on at most $k$ fresh copies and no quantum memory is retained between blocks. We prove a lower bound matching the upper bound in [arXiv:2510.07788]. Thus the copy complexity of estimating an arbitrary $d$-dimensional state to trace distance $ε$ is, up to absolute constant factors, $\max\{d^3/(\sqrt{k}ε^2),d^2/ε^2\}$ for every $k$ and all sufficiently small $ε$. This removes the earlier restriction that $k$ be small as a function of the accuracy. The lower bound applies to arbitrary measurements within each block and adaptive choices between blocks. The lower bound already applies in a small neighborhood of any state whose smallest eigenvalue is of order $1/d$, even when the center is known. The main ingredient is a uniform Fisher information bound for one measurement block that depends only on the smallest eigenvalue of the state. The proof avoids the perturbative expansion responsible for the restriction in [arXiv:2402.16353]. Fano's inequality for metric balls and a log-Sobolev comparison between mutual and Fisher information then reduce the adaptive protocol to this block bound [arXiv:1607.00550, arXiv:1902.08582].

title: CPL: A Compact C-like Systems Language with Explicit Low-Level Control
abstract: This paper presents Cordell Programming Language (CPL), a compact C-like systems language that retains C's direct access to memory, layout, and machine interfaces while experimenting with a smaller grammar and selected conveniences from newer languages. Also this paper studies whether C-like are more convenient to use for compiler experiments than modern approaches and paradigms. While the language and compiler provide primitive values, pointers, arrays, containers with methods, unions, generic functions, overloads, entry-point and section control, system calls, and inline assembly, they do not provide high-level constructs such as classes, built-in methods, a standard library, or memory protection. The article describes the language design, compiler pipeline, target backends, static-analysis architecture, and OS-facing use cases, then evaluates the prototype backend with reproducible x86_64 and i386 microbenchmarks against C compiler baselines. The obtained results suggest that the compiler can produce code comparable to that produced by production compilers such as GCC and Clang, as well as by small compilers such as TinyC and SmallerC.

title: MMTClinic: Multimodal, Multilingual Time Series Question Answering and Reasoning Benchmark for Clinical Domain
abstract: Time-series data in clinical settings is crucial for capturing dynamic changes in a patient's health over time, enabling timely diagnosis, personalized treatment, and early detection of critical events. However, the development of clinically reliable and linguistically inclusive medical AI systems remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the lack of multimodal, multilingual, and time-series-grounded benchmarks that reflect the complexity of real-world clinical scenarios. To fill this gap, we present MMTClinic, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on complex reasoning and question-answering tasks involving clinical time-series. MMTClinic combines text, medical images, and multivariate physiological signals and includes 30,000 QA pairs (15,000 multiple choice questions (MCQs) and 15,000 open-ended questions) across five languages: English, Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, and Tamil. These questions cover three important clinical tasks---mortality prediction, heart rate forecasting, and SOFA score estimation. We evaluate 13 state-of-the-art LLMs in zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought settings. Our evaluation reveals notable differences in model performance across tasks, languages, and modalities, highlighting current limitations in clinical reasoning capabilities. MMTClinic provides a valuable resource for advancing multilingual, multimodal, and time-series-aware medical AI research. The dataset will be made publicly available on successful acceptance of the work.

title: A Study on The Impact of Generative AI on Investment Decision Making at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.
abstract: This study, titled "A Study on the Impact of Generative AI on Investment Decision Making at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.," evaluates use case allocations, research analyst productivity gains, Assets Under Management (AUM) expansion, and financial feasibility of Generative AI (GenAI) integration in institutional wealth management and retail equity advisory. Wealth management firms face high research overhead, where equity report drafting represents 42% and portfolio chatbots account for 28% of GenAI applications. A five-year project lifecycle (2021-2025) of an enterprise GenAI research platform at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. is evaluated using capital budgeting parameters: Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Payback Period (PBP), and Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR). Quantitative analysis reveals that deploying a GenAI research copilot reduces valuation report preparation time to 2.1 hours compared to 18.5 hours under manual research. title: Title: Parallel Algorithm for Quantum State Collapse Analysis
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, and its analysis is a critical task in quantum algorithm design and verification. Traditional methods struggle to handle the immense complexity of quantum systems due to the exponential growth of state space. This paper introduces a novel parallel algorithm designed to efficiently analyze the collapse of quantum states, utilizing distributed computing techniques to rapidly explore the vast state space and pinpoint key collapse pathways. The algorithm's core mechanism involves distributing the analysis across multiple cores and nodes, leveraging advanced quantum computing techniques to expedite the evaluation of various parameters. This approach promises to dramatically reduce computational time and enhance the ability to identify crucial collapse events, ultimately improving the robustness and reliability of quantum algorithms. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum state collapse analysis and offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and scalable quantum system modeling.

title: Title: Quantum Complexity Theory - Entanglement-Driven Verification
abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) offers a novel framework for verifying the correctness of complex mathematical proofs, moving beyond traditional verification methods reliant on computational complexity. This paper introduces a new protocol leveraging quantum entanglement to simultaneously assess multiple steps within a proof, dramatically increasing the probability of detecting subtle inconsistencies. The core mechanism involves creating entangled qubits to explore the proof space in a fundamentally different way, revealing logical errors with significantly enhanced precision. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis of a simplified example, highlighting its potential to revolutionize the verification process. The research explores the inherent challenges and opportunities presented by quantum mechanics in this domain, emphasizing the potential for a paradigm shift in mathematical assurance.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum State Transfer and Mitigation
abstract: Quantum state transfer and mitigation are critical challenges in quantum computing, requiring efficient and robust methods to handle complex quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology framework for quantum state transfer and mitigation, leveraging the inherent self-adaptive properties of quantum topology. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the topology to facilitate rapid state shifts and mitigates potential errors arising from quantum decoherence. The core mechanism centers on employing a series of iterative transformations within the dynamic topology to minimize the impact of environmental noise. The advantages of this approach include enhanced efficiency, improved stability, and the potential for scaling quantum computations. This research contributes to a fundamental shift in the design of quantum algorithms, offering a promising path toward more practical and reliable quantum computing.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic logic and the proof by contradiction method to establish rigorous mathematical reasoning. The core principle is to treat every statement as a probabilistic truth, allowing for self-correction based on probabilities. This approach offers a fundamentally different method for mathematical investigation, potentially surpassing the limitations of traditional proofs. The paper details the design of the Quantum Probability Logic system, its underlying mathematical principles, and its potential applications across diverse mathematical domains. We explore the advantages and challenges of this new methodology, emphasizing its capacity to provide a more dependable foundation for formal reasoning.

title: Dynamic Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol designed to enhance security by adapting to fluctuating environmental noise. Traditional QKD protocols often operate under the assumption of constant noise, which is rarely true in real-world scenarios. This protocol leverages quantum feedback control to monitor and respond to changes in the noise level, thereby improving key generation rates and overall security. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting key distribution parameters based on real-time noise measurements. The design addresses a critical limitation of existing protocols and offers a more robust and practical approach to secure key exchange. This work outlines the theoretical framework, key equations, and the proposed algorithm for this dynamic QKD protocol.

title: An Enhanced Newton Downhill Optimizer for High-Dimensional Optimization and Thermal–Pumped-Storage Economic Dispatch
abstract: The Newton Downhill Optimizer (NDO) provides a compact derivative-free search framework, but its random dimension mask, uniform treatment of individuals, and limited use of supplementary global-best candidates may restrict performance on high-dimensional problems. This study proposes an Enhanced Newton Downhill Optimizer (ENDO) that incorporates three mechanisms: an adaptive dimension mask, a DE/rand/2-based greedy mutation for inferior individuals, and dynamic-boundary opposition-based best guidance. ENDO was evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark at 10, 30, 50, and 100 dimensions. The primary comparison involved nine representative optimizers, and an additional 100-dimensional comparison was conducted with six advanced optimizers. In the primary 100-dimensional tests, ENDO ranked first on 18 of 29 functions, remained among the top three on 26 functions, and achieved an average rank of 1.79. In the additional comparison, ENDO ranked third with an average rank of 3.52. Across the four dimensions, its average ranks were 1.79, 1.66, 1.38, and 1.79, indicating stable performance under changes in problem scale. ENDO was further applied to a 168-dimensional thermal–pumped-storage economic dispatch problem, where it achieved the lowest mean operating cost, the best average rank of 1.87, and a feasibility rate of 100% over 30 independent runs. Statistical analyses further supported the competitiveness of ENDO across the benchmark and engineering evaluations. These results show that ENDO improves the sustained search capability of NDO and provides competitive performance for complex high-dimensional and constrained optimization problems.

title: Advances in time-independent Hamiltonian simulation algorithms
abstract: Abstract Quantum simulation is a rapidly advancing field poised to revolutionize our understanding of complex quantum systems by harnessing the unique capabilities of quantum computers. In this review, we present a concise overview of key developments in quantum simulation algorithms, with a focus on time-independent digital Hamiltonian simulation of quantum dynamics. We review seminal methods—from traditional Trotter formulas to techniques such as truncated Taylor series combined with the linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing. Additionally, we examine error analyses and recent innovations that enhance the efficiency and accuracy of quantum simulations.

title: Adaptive Cost-Sensitive Machine Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation Failure Prediction: When Not All Errors Are Equal
abstract: Autonomous robot navigation failures differ not only in categorical severity but also in the physical context in which they occur. A near-miss at low speed under reliable sensing is not equivalent to the same event during rapid motion, close obstacle approach or degraded perception. This paper reframes navigation failure prediction as consequence-sensitive forecasting. We first establish a fixed baseline in which training weights are modulated by categorical severity, then introduce an adaptive extension defining a state-dependent consequence function combining severity with normalised velocity, obstacle proximity and sensing uncertainty, together with a risk-sensitivity term that rises as conditions deteriorate. We evaluate on 2,000 simulated differential-drive episodes (~1,000,000 timesteps) using episode-level GroupKFold, with external validation on the UCI SCITOS G5 dataset. Fixed weighting raises Logistic Regression high-severity recall from 0.851 to 0.985 and reduces missed consequence cost from 1,940 to 313; the adaptive extension reaches 0.998 and 82. Under matched false-positive conditions, however, the discriminative advantage is modest (0.986 versus 0.984), so most of the gain reflects a more conservative operating point rather than better ranking. The effect is consistent across all five folds and stable across a threefold span of context coefficients. Because the primary simulation produced no collisions, we add a controlled extension in which 108 of 600 episodes terminate in contact: collision recall rises from 0.850 to 0.966 (fixed) and 0.984 (adaptive), with missed collision cost falling from 1,000 to 105, at false-positive rates of 0.413 and 0.799, respectively. Context-dependent consequence modelling thus provides a principled mechanism for allocating conservatism by physical risk.

title: Fundamental Limits of Quantum Metrology Beyond Fixed Causal Order
abstract: Quantum metrology with indefinite causal order (ICO) has attracted intense interest due to its potential to surpass the limitations of conventional fixed-order strategies. A key open question is whether ICO can fundamentally enhance asymptotic precision scaling. In this work, we bridge this gap for the estimation of a single parameter encoded in $N$ identical uses of a finite-dimensional quantum channel. We first establish a universal Heisenberg-scaling upper bound for the full general ICO process-matrix class and show that for unitary channels its optimal quantum Fisher information (QFI) coincides exactly with that of parallel strategies. Most significantly, an asymptotically tight (AT) bound is derived to close the remaining possibility of an asymptotic ICO advantage by showing that general ICO and optimal parallel strategies have exactly the same leading QFI coefficient in both the SQL and Heisenberg regimes. title: Aplaud: Adaptive Personalized Low-Rank Decomposition for User-Specific LLM
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of personalized survey response prediction using fine-tuned large language models (LLMs). This task poses unique challenges: limited per-user training data, scalability of model storage, and the need to exploit shared structure across survey questions. To address these issues, we propose Aplaud (Adaptive Personalized Low-rank and User-specific Nested Decomposition), a lightweight and scalable framework for LLM personalization. Aplaud extends the LoRA paradigm by separating adaptation into a frozen, shared low-rank basis and a compact user-specific correction, augmented with a rank-one residual for finer personalization. To further reduce per-user parameter cost and mitigate overfitting, the correction matrix can be factorized into an even lower-rank form. Empirical results demonstrate that Aplaud achieves efficient, scalable personalization across users while outperforming state-of-the-art LoRA-based personalized LLM approaches in both generalization and inference efficiency.

abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive algorithm for optimization, leveraging the principles of a self-adaptive feedback loop. We introduce a 'Self-Adapting Feedback Loop' (SFL) mechanism that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters to optimize complex systems, effectively mitigating uncertainty and enhancing robustness. The SFL approach significantly improves algorithm performance compared to static parameter tuning methods. This research emphasizes the algorithm's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions, offering a more flexible and reliable solution for optimization problems. We explore the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of this algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness in a simulated scenario.

title: Bayesian Network with Dynamic Prior Refinement via Bayesian Interpolation
abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian Network architecture designed to enhance predictive accuracy across a wide range of scenarios by incorporating dynamic prior refinement via Bayesian Interpolation. Traditional Bayesian Networks rely on fixed priors, which can be suboptimal when data reveals significant uncertainty. This work proposes a mechanism that iteratively refines the network's prior distribution based on observed data, leading to more robust and adaptable predictions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on diverse datasets, showcasing significant improvements in predictive capability compared to existing methods. The core of our design involves a Bayesian Interpolation algorithm that progressively updates the probability distributions, effectively exploring the data space and reducing the influence of initial assumptions.

title: WhatsApp Business for Restaurants
abstract: Cutoffs, covers, and the order the kitchen cannot cook A food order accepted at the wrong minute cannot be rescued by any message sent afterwards, because the constraint is a prep window measured from the stove and not a conversation measured from the phone. Restaurants running orders through a chat window fail on timing rather than on service. The thread accepts an order the moment a customer sends it, while the kitchen can only accept an order it can still cook, plate and hand off before the dish stops being what was sold. Those two clocks are not the same and nothing in a chat window shows the difference. A restaurant that publishes cutoffs, counts its covers per service, and closes items before they are claimed is not being stricter with customers; it is making the phone tell the truth about the kitchen. The remedy is entirely inside the restaurant's control, which makes late food a property of its own accepting habits. Audiences: The kitchen accepting the order — Accepts every message that arrives because refusing one feels like refusing money, then discovers at the pass that four of the eleven orders taken for one lunch cannot physically be made in the time left. The cook watching a service go wrong — Is mid-service with a spike already accepted, food going cold on the pass, and a phone filling with customers asking where their order is. Every minute spent replying is a minute not spent cooking, and both are already short. The operator setting the terms before the rush — Has never counted covers per service, has no cutoff written anywhere a customer can read, and discovers the limits of the kitchen only by exceeding them on the busiest night of the month. Note: written from Indonesian operator context. Frameworks apply broadly to other emerging-market and SME settings.

title: Topology-Based Formal Verification of Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: This paper introduces a novel technique for formally verifying the security of cryptographic protocols using topological principles, specifically focusing on analyzing network connectivity and relationships to detect vulnerabilities. Traditional security proofs often rely on complex mathematical models and assumptions, while this approach leverages the inherent structure of networks to provide a more robust and automated verification process. We propose a framework that utilizes graph theory and topological invariants to rigorously prove the correctness of cryptographic algorithms, offering a significant advancement in the field of formal verification. The core mechanism involves developing a mathematical framework that analyzes network topology to identify potential weaknesses, ultimately enhancing the security of cryptographic systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology, specifically a genetic algorithm (GA) adapted to dynamically adjust its parameters based on the input data. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in scenarios with varying data. This algorithm leverages the concept of dynamic topology, allowing the GA to reconfigure its search space and explore the solution space more effectively, potentially leading to improved convergence and performance. The proposed method focuses on enhancing the algorithm's adaptability and robustness through the manipulation of its core structure. This paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and a comprehensive analysis of its advantages over existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism revolves around the continuous adaptation of the genetic operators to reflect the changing characteristics of the problem, resulting in optimized solutions.

title: Symbolic Regression with Deep Bayesian Networks
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to uncover mathematical expressions that accurately describe a given dataset. Traditional symbolic regression methods frequently encounter difficulties when dealing with complex, non-linear relationships, often resulting in simplified or less accurate models. This work proposes a novel approach combining deep Bayesian Networks (DBNs) with symbolic regression techniques. The core idea is to utilize the representational power of deep learning, specifically DBNs, to explore a wider range of potential mathematical models and subsequently refine these models through symbolic regression. We hypothesize that the hierarchical structure of DBNs, combined with the search capabilities of symbolic regression, will lead to the discovery of more complex, accurate, and ultimately more interpretable mathematical expressions. This approach offers a potential solution to the limitations of existing symbolic regression tools, particularly when faced with highly intricate datasets. The presented methodology is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and anticipated benefits, without empirical testing.

title: Dynamic Symbolic Regression for Evolving Systems
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its traditional application is limited when dealing with systems exhibiting temporal dynamics – systems where the underlying mathematical relationships change over time. This work introduces a novel dynamic symbolic regression (DSR) algorithm designed specifically for evolving systems. The core of the DSR approach lies in a continuous learning process that integrates both historical and streaming data. We employ a temporal Bayesian model to represent uncertainty and facilitate adaptation. This model allows the system to not only identify equations that accurately describe the current state of the system but also to track and adjust to changes in those relationships. The algorithm's architecture and methodology are presented, focusing on the key components: data ingestion, equation generation, Bayesian model updating, and equation selection. The resulting DSR system demonstrates improved performance compared to static SR methods in scenarios with evolving system dynamics. This addresses a critical limitation in existing SR techniques and opens possibilities for modeling and understanding complex, time-varying systems.

title: Title: Emergent Complexity from Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) represents a monumental leap in computational security, offering the potential for vastly more robust quantum computations than classical systems. However, the intricate interplay of quantum states and their fragility makes precise control and prediction of complex, self-organizing behavior a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel framework, "Guided Evolution," predicated on the active utilization of quantum error correction to induce and stabilize emergent complexity within a system, ultimately leading to enhanced robustness. We aim to construct a model that anticipates and mitigates the inherent instability of complex quantum systems, paving the way for new computational paradigms. This work explores a method of strategically manipulating quantum states to encourage self-organization and minimize the impact of errors, demonstrating a pathway toward a fundamentally new approach to understanding and controlling complex quantum behavior. The core mechanism revolves around dynamically adjusting quantum states to steer the evolution of a system, minimizing the likelihood of detrimental errors.

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a critical bottleneck in the training of reinforcement learning (RL) agents. Manually searching for optimal hyperparameters is a laborious and often ineffective process. This paper proposes a novel approach that leverages meta-reinforcement learning (MRL) coupled with Bayesian optimization to automate this process. We train a meta-RL agent, referred to as the "meta-controller," whose objective is to learn and execute effective hyperparameter tuning strategies for a target RL agent. Bayesian optimization is then employed within the meta-controller to efficiently explore the vast hyperparameter space, selecting the best configurations for the target RL agent. Our methodology offers an automated, adaptive, and potentially significantly faster route to training high-performing RL agents compared to traditional manual tuning methods. The core idea is to learn a policy for tuning policies, creating a nested optimization problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, highlighting its ability to rapidly identify optimal hyperparameters across diverse RL environments. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of MRL and Bayesian optimization, leading to a robust and scalable solution for hyperparameter optimization in RL.

title: Title: Adaptive Correction of Quantum Error Correcting Codes
abstract: Quantum error correcting codes are crucial for reliable quantum information processing. Traditional methods rely on computationally intensive error correction matrices, which pose challenges in terms of resource consumption and complexity. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum error correction utilizing adaptive correction mechanisms, leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states to streamline the correction process and minimize computational overhead. We introduce a quantum error correcting code architecture that dynamically adjusts the quantum state during the error correction cycle, effectively reducing the computational burden without relying on pre-computed error correction matrices. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the topological properties of the quantum state to dynamically adjust the state, facilitating efficient and secure error correction. This work represents a significant advancement towards more efficient and robust quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Algorithms' Adaptive Optimization and Expansion
abstract: Quantum algorithms hold immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, and a key challenge in their development lies in optimizing their performance across diverse input datasets. We introduce a quantum algorithm that adapts its parameter adjustments based on the characteristics of the input data, achieving improved efficiency and performance through real-time parameter tuning. This system, termed "Quantum Adaptive Tuning," leverages a combination of quantum optimization techniques with a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism. The core mechanism is to iteratively refine the quantum algorithm's parameters to maximize the likelihood of finding optimal solutions. We present a theoretical analysis and initial experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this work and future research directions.

The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting model parameters based on the data distribution, minimizing overfitting and enhancing generalization across diverse datasets. We propose a method that utilizes tensor operations to represent and manipulate data, enabling efficient and adaptable optimization strategies. This approach aims to improve the performance of machine learning models, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets and complex data distributions. The algorithm is structured to systematically refine the model's parameters, resulting in improved accuracy and robustness. The work demonstrates the efficacy of this novel method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential for advancing machine learning practices.

title: 基于自适应机器学习的系统优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel system optimization approach leveraging adaptive machine learning models. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be cumbersome and inefficient, particularly in complex scenarios. Our proposed algorithm employs a self-adjusting machine learning model parameter adjustment mechanism, allowing the system to dynamically optimize model accuracy and performance. The core mechanism centers around automated parameter refinement through an adaptive learning process, offering a robust and automated solution for system optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's key components, its advantages, and potential applications.

title: Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation and data processing. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement in computational architecture, specifically focusing on its application within quantum machine learning. The core claim posits that the unique properties of entanglement, particularly its inherent parallelism and non-classical correlations, can be harnessed to enable significantly enhanced parallel computation capabilities, and this capability will be utilized to advance quantum machine learning algorithms. This work explores the creation of quantum entanglement as a foundational element for computation, details quantum algorithms designed to exploit entanglement, and investigates the potential advantages quantum machine learning offers compared to classical approaches. The paper presents a novel framework for designing quantum algorithms centered around entanglement, demonstrating preliminary results that suggest a significant shift in the landscape of parallel computation, with a particular emphasis on quantum machine learning.

title: Quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and real matrix-vector query problems
abstract: We (the author and the AI systems that did the heavy lifting) show that the quantum query complexity of minimizing a convex function over a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with evaluation and membership queries is $\tildeΩ(n)$, nearly matching the best known upper bound. In particular, we show this even for quadratic minimization, which is equivalent to inverting an $n \times n$ real matrix using matrix-vector queries. We also show linear or nearly linear lower bounds on the quantum query complexity of computing the trace, the sign of the determinant, and the magnitude of the determinant of a real matrix in the matrix-vector query model. We use a novel quantum lower bound technique, the determinantal witness method, based on identifying a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and that correlates well with the function being computed.

title: Whose record is this? Diagnosing and authorizing record use in personalized multimodal models
abstract: Contextualized visual personalization can retrieve a true record yet apply it to the wrong visual subject. We formalize when a record may condition an answer as \emph{record authorization}: subject presence ($P$), record-edge validity ($E$), and answer support ($S$) must all hold. We call violations visual memory misbinding (VMM). We construct RecordAuth-Diag, a 3,690-case matched diagnostic suite that changes one image--record edge while holding the query, question, record text, and image multiset fixed. Card removal and nonce relabeling attribute these failures to supplied records. Raw-bank failures span Qwen-, Phi-, and Gemma-family interfaces: Gemma-3-4B-IT reaches 63.69\% local unauthorized use at 25.75\% clean recall. CoViP remains at 26.02\%, versus 22.49\% for its Qwen backbone at similar clean recall. Typed pre-generation authorization reduces Qwen card exposure on RecordAuth-Diag from 43.63\% to 3.06\%, while positive recall changes from 86.26\% to 60.90\%. Full $P\wedge E\wedge S$ validation uses 560 localized DAVIS cases: top-1 relevance and typed authorization have comparable release (28.93\% and 28.39\%) but 6.79\% and 0.89\% unsafe release, respectively. Of the 33 additional unsafe cases removed, 27 are support, 4 edge, 2 clean, and 0 boundary cases. Thus the observed increment is an $E\wedge S$ decision dominated by support, not an edge check alone. Appearance supplies $E$ evidence only conditional on $P$; authenticated subject tokens instantiate the missing presence witness as a sufficiency control. The claims concern the evaluated contracts, not natural prevalence, consent, or visual identity

title: Representation Redundancy and Structural Complexity in Finite-Field Inversion
abstract: The representation chosen for a mathematical operation can affect both its algebraic form and its empirical learning difficulty. We study this phenomenon for inversion over \(\mathbb F_{2^n}\), with field elements expressed in varying ordered \(\mathbb F_2\)-bases. We prove that two ordered bases induce the same coordinate inversion map if and only if they belong to the same Galois orbit. Since every orbit has size \(n\), the correspondence between ordered bases and distinct inversion maps is exactly \(n\)-to-one. We then analyze three Boolean formulations of inversion. The reference formulation has algebraic degree \(n-1\) and joint ANF leap \(1\), the mixed representation formulation has degree \(2(n-1)\) and joint ANF leap \(2\), and the complete raw formulation has degree at most \(3(n-1)\) and joint ANF leap at least \(n\). Exhaustive computations agree with the theoretical results and bounds in the cases considered. Controlled experiments with multilayer perceptrons show the same ordering in learning difficulty, while Galois orbit redundancy provides only a limited generalization benefit under the tested conditions. These results show that exact redundancy among representations can coexist with changes in Boolean structure and learning behavior when the representation is exposed as part of the input.

title: CPU-only maximum verification suite for qector-decoder-v3 1.0.0 under an Enterprise license.
abstract: CPU-only maximum verification suite for qector-decoder-v3 1.0.0 under an Enterprise license. This deposit contains the complete pytest suite, machine report, and supporting artifacts used to confirm syndrome-faithful batch decoding on CPU across eleven code families and twenty-two decoder backends. Distances from 3 to the Enterprise cap of 63 were exercised. All 376 tests passed with zero failures. Key results- 100 % syndrome faithfulness (H c = s mod 2) on every checked shot- Code families: repetition, ring, rotated surface, unrotated surface, toric, heavy-hex, colour code, hypergraph product, bicycle, bivariate bicycle, and arbitrary parity-check matrices- Decoder backends include Union-Find, Fast Union-Find, Blossom, Sparse Blossom, BP-OSD, Hybrid Cascade, AutoDecoder, Space-Time, Streaming, Sliding-Window, and related variants- Shot ladder from 1 to 1 000 000; extreme-shot and robustness cases included- Enterprise distance cap verified: d = 63 accepted, d = 64 correctly rejected with PermissionError- Host: AMD EPYC 7V12 (4 cores / 8 logical), 28 GiB RAM, Windows 11, Python 3.11, pure CPU (no CUDA / OpenCL) Contents- Full pytest suite (test_00 to test_11 plus conftest and harness)- CPU_MAX_REPORT.json (structured machine and result metadata)- QECTOR_CPU_MAX_ZENODO_PRO_REPORT.pdf and its SHA-256 checksum- zenodo_deposit_metadata.json Reproducibility noteAn active Enterprise license key is required to execute the full suite and to reach distance 63. Community and Pro tiers are limited to lower distances by design. Throughput numbers are host-specific and are reported only as measured on the listed hardware; they are not claimed as portable performance guarantees. title: Impersonation Ambiguity as a Security Signal: A Quantitative Framework for Role-Play vs. Malicious Impersonation Detection in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support persona adoption and character role-play as a first-class, legitimate usecase; creative writing assistants, companion chatbots, and educational simulations all depend on it. Yet the same mechanism isthe substrate of one of the most persistent jailbreak families in the literature, and it is exploited directly for social-engineering-style impersonation of real individuals, brands, and authorities. Prior security systems typically treat “impersonation” as asingle binary label, and our own earlier work on the SemGuard gateway found empirically that this label is the most contestedcategory any moderation system can assign: three independent frontier-model judges agreed on only 3 of 166 generated imper-sonation examples (a 98.2% inter-judge rejection/disagreement rate), far higher than any other threat category in that study.This paper treats that disagreement not as annotation noise to be minimized away, but as a measurable security signal in itsown right. We formalize the distinction between benign role-play (persona adoption bounded by fictional framing, consent, andnon-deceptive intent) and malicious impersonation (persona adoption intended to deceive a third party, extract value, or evadeattribution) as a multi-dimensional classification problem rather than a single decision boundary. We propose a quantitativeframework – the Impersonation Ambiguity Index (IAI) – that scores any persona-bearing input along four independent axes:target realism, deceptive intent, consent/context boundedness, and downstream actionability. We show how this index can beoperationalized on top of an LLM-as-Judge annotation pipeline, propose an evaluation protocol using multi-judge Fleiss’ κ peraxis rather than per label, and outline how the resulting ambiguity scores can be fed back into a semantic security gateway (inthe style of Triple-Anchor architectures) as a fifth, uncertainty-aware anchor rather than forcing a premature binary decision.We situate this proposal against the jailbreak, persona-prompting, and AI-enabled social-engineering literatures, and arguethat ambiguity-aware, axis-decomposed labeling is a necessary next step for any multilingual or cross-cultural moderation sys-tem, where role-play norms and what counts as “impersonation” vary sharply across languages and communities. This paperpresents the framework and evaluation protocol together with an initial n = 40 pilot run (Section V-E); full-scale validation onthe expanded, dialect-stratified dataset remains future work.

title: 量子模拟的拓扑场论建模
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a powerful approach to modeling complex quantum phenomena, including those found in topological field theories. This paper explores a novel quantum simulation method designed to precisely map topological field theory's geometry to quantum states, enabling the study of topological field theory's dynamic evolution and its implications for physical system behavior. The core mechanism centers on mapping geometric information directly onto quantum states, utilizing quantum simulation to unravel the intricate dynamics of topological fields. This approach addresses limitations of traditional simulation techniques, providing a more accurate and detailed representation of these systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Chaos in Differential Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive chaos to differential geometry, aiming to develop a computational algorithm that dynamically adjusts the complexity of a model based on observed error signals. Inspired by the emergent behavior of chaotic systems, we propose a reinforcement learning framework where the model parameters are optimized iteratively. The core mechanism involves a self-optimizing model that mimics the dynamics of chaotic systems, leading to improved modeling and prediction capabilities for complex physical phenomena. This work addresses a critical limitation in traditional differential geometry models: the reliance on static, simplified geometries. The proposed approach offers a pathway towards generating more realistic and robust representations of physical systems, potentially unlocking new insights and predictive tools.

title: 基于非线性拓扑的量子计算的拓扑优化算法
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but the design and optimization of quantum circuits often face significant challenges, particularly in the context of complex quantum algorithms. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computing, utilizing a modified version of the topological optimization algorithm, to address these challenges. We introduce a new framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to dynamically adjust the structure of quantum circuits, enabling more efficient and robust optimization. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the non-linear nature of topological spaces to guide the evolution of quantum states, ultimately improving the performance of quantum algorithms. This research explores the potential of this approach to tackle specific problems in quantum information processing and highlights its advantages over existing methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Temporal Quantum State Collapse (ATQCC) for Simulation
abstract: Adaptive Temporal Quantum State Collapse (ATQCC) presents a novel method for dynamically adjusting the collapse of quantum states within simulation environments, aiming to improve the fidelity of long-term simulations. Current state collapse techniques often lack adaptive control, leading to instability and inaccuracies. ATQCC leverages a self-adjusting quantum state collapse algorithm based on the system's dynamics, offering a potential for more stable and accurate simulations. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of ATQCC, detailing the core mechanism and its potential impact on quantum simulation fidelity.

title: Code and data for a controlled audit of the ann-thyroid benchmark
abstract: Code, raw data and generated results for a controlled audit of the UCI ann-thyroid multiclass benchmark. Rebuilds the cohort table from the raw files, establishes the class semantics at record level against the sibling files distributed in the same UCI directory, and evaluates whether reported performance differences between feature-selection methods and class-balancing strategies are large enough to matter.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Network for Fractal Analysis (DCNA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Constraint Network for Fractal Analysis (DCNA), a novel framework for generating and analyzing fractal networks. DCNA utilizes a deep neural network to learn the structure of fractal networks, allowing for automated discovery of underlying patterns and relationships. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic constraint system, which iteratively adjusts the network's structure to reveal emergent properties and enhance the search for fractal patterns. The system's ability to dynamically generate and analyze fractal networks offers a significant advancement in fractal research and offers a powerful tool for exploring complex mathematical structures. The DCNA system's design incorporates a novel constraint mechanism that allows for the exploration of a broader range of fractal characteristics.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Reorganization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Dynamic Quantum State Reorganization (DQSR), designed to achieve dynamic reorganization of quantum states leveraging quantum entanglement and controlled decoherence. The core concept mirrors biological gene recombination, utilizing entanglement as a "template" and manipulating decoherence to perform precise "cuts" and "stitches" within the quantum state space. Unlike existing methods, DQSR aims to address the limitations of inefficiency and lack of control in quantum state manipulation. The algorithm is predicated on the fundamental principle that quantum states, while fragile, can be precisely altered through careful management of their interaction with the environment. The presented framework outlines the mathematical formalism and key operational steps, providing a theoretical foundation for future exploration and potential implementation. The algorithm's effectiveness hinges on the precise control of decoherence rates, offering a pathway to constructing complex quantum states from simpler ones. This work establishes a new approach to quantum state manipulation, with implications for quantum computation, quantum information processing, and potentially, novel quantum materials design.

evidence.abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Dynamic Quantum State Reorganization (DQSR), designed to achieve dynamic reorganization of quantum states leveraging quantum entanglement and controlled decoherence. The core concept mirrors biological gene recombination, utilizing entanglement as a "template" and manipulating decoherence to perform precise "cuts" and "stitches" within the quantum state space. Unlike existing methods, DQSR aims to address the limitations of inefficiency and lack of control in quantum state manipulation. The algorithm is predicated on the fundamental principle that quantum states, while fragile, can be precisely altered through careful management of their interaction with the environment. The presented framework outlines the mathematical formalism and key operational steps, providing a theoretical foundation for future exploration and potential implementation. The algorithm's effectiveness hinges on the precise control of decoherence rates, offering a pathway to constructing complex quantum states from simpler ones. This work establishes a new approach to quantum state manipulation, with implications for quantum computation, quantum information processing, and potentially, novel quantum materials design.

title: Temporal Relational Reasoning with Recurrent Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal relational reasoning by integrating recurrent neural networks with Bayesian networks. The core idea is to model the dynamic evolution of relationships within a dataset using a recurrent Bayesian network (RBN). Traditional Bayesian networks represent static relationships, while this work addresses the challenge of capturing temporal dependencies and changes in these relationships over time. The proposed method employs recurrent neural networks to learn the sequential dependencies within the RBN, effectively capturing how relationships shift and adapt based on past observations. The resulting model allows for more accurate inference and prediction in scenarios where relational data exhibits temporal dynamics. We formalize this approach with a mathematical framework, outlining the key components and the recurrent update rule for the Bayesian network. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and a discussion of potential applications, highlighting its ability to handle complex, time-varying relational data. The core of the research lies in the ability to model the evolution of relationships, represented as a recurrent Bayesian network, allowing for dynamic inference and prediction.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Compression and Multi-Variable Functional Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to information compression and multi-variable functional learning leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entangled states for efficient data representation, effectively reducing redundancy and enabling accurate estimation of multi-variable functions. We propose a framework where multi-variable data is encoded into entangled states, facilitating a significant reduction in storage requirements while simultaneously providing a robust method for learning complex relationships. The theoretical underpinnings rely on the superposition and correlation properties inherent in entangled systems. The system is mathematically formulated using tensor networks and density matrix representations to describe the entangled state. The key contribution lies in the combined application of entanglement-based compression and the subsequent use of this compressed representation for learning multi-variable functions. The proposed method offers potential advantages over classical approaches, particularly in scenarios dealing with high-dimensional data and complex dependencies. The presented framework provides a foundation for future research in quantum machine learning and data analysis.

title: Title: Non-Standard Graph Representation – Representing the Human Brain as a Dynamic Graph Network
abstract: This paper explores the potential of novel graph representations to model the human brain, focusing on incorporating dynamic connections and feedback loops. Current models often struggle with the complexity of neural network activity, necessitating a more refined approach. We propose a graph representation where nodes represent neural circuits and edges represent synaptic connections, and the graph evolves over time based on activity. The core mechanism involves implementing a dynamic graph representation that captures the intricate feedback mechanisms inherent in brain function. This research aims to provide a foundational framework for exploring and understanding complex cognitive processes through the lens of dynamic graph networks. The investigation will address the limitations of existing representations and highlight the benefits of this approach in modeling neural activity.

title: ThreatLens: Claim-Level Grounding Verification for LLM-Extracted Cyber Threat Intelligence
abstract: Large language models are increasingly proposed for automating cyber threat intelligence (CTI) extraction, but existing benchmarks evaluate them with precision-style accuracy metrics against static gold labels. I argue this measurement approach is unsafe for operational deployment, and I present ThreatLens, an open-source pipeline that performs deterministic, claim-level grounding verification of LLM-extracted CTI against three authorities: the National Vulnerability Database, MITRE ATT&CK STIX data, and the source document itself. Every atomic claim (CVE, indicator of compromise, ATT&CK technique, threat actor, malware family) receives one of five verdicts under a taxonomy that separates fabricated entities from entities that are real but ungrounded in the source, mislabeled metadata, and claims that are simply unverifiable because no authority can confirm them. I evaluate five open-weight models on 94 CISA advisories published after the models' training cutoffs, plus two indicator-list CTI events. Four findings emerge. (i) Hallucination is task-dependent rather than model-intrinsic: Nemotron-3-Super 120B scores 0.00% [95% CI: 0.00%, 0.52%] on indicator-copying tasks and 6.39% [4.65%, 8.73%] on narrative advisories requiring inference. (ii) Precision metrics conceal silent failure: Nemotron-3-nano 30B returned well-formed but empty extractions on 100.0% [72.2%, 100.0%] of its successful runs over CVE-bearing advisories, which a precision-only benchmark would report as flawless. Even Nemotron-3-Super 120B silently returns nothing on 11.2% [7.0%, 17.4%] of CVE-bearing advisories. (iii) Two reproducible failure modes appear at temperature 0: parametric-memory CVE imports and systematic ATT&CK sub-technique confabulation. (iv) Following NIST's April 2026 decision to abandon universal NVD enrichment, existence checking against vulnerability registries fails precisely on the freshest advisories: 9 of 11 CVEs cited verbatim in same-week ICS advisories were absent from both NVD and CVE.org. I further report the verifier's own audit trail: five classes of verifier false positive discovered by manual adjudication and fixed under regression test, which I argue should be a standard reporting requirement for automated CTI evaluation. Code, corpus manifests, and per-claim verdicts are released.
